The Sun enters Scorpio October 23 at 2:38 AM PDT / 5:38 AM EDT.

This is one of my favorite times of the year! Scorpio is my sister sign on the zodiac and dominates my big 3. TheHoodwitch.com and my first book, Blood Sex Magic, were both born under Scorpio. It’s a season that always brings me back to myself, reminding me of who I am at my core, my true essence.

Scorpio is deeply connected to sex, death, and magic, so you already know why I love this season. Pluto, its modern ruler, is named after the god of the underworld. There’s power in what’s hidden, including the parts of ourselves we’d rather keep private. Plutonian energy can bring up jealousy, obsession, and desires we don’t always know what to do with. Be honest about what’s coming up for you.

With Venus and Mercury retrograde this season, there’s a lot to unpack around love, money, and our relationships. Some of us are revisiting things we thought we were done with. There’s beauty in facing yourself without hiding from your shadow. 

Stop dimming your light just to make others comfortable, and remember your own fckin’ power!

HAPPY FULL MOON IN TAURUS ♉︎🌕

There is absolutely nothing unspiritual about wanting a beautiful life, a safe home, and enough money to enjoy both. As a Taurus, I will always stand by that. 💅🏾 

In Greek mythology, Taurus is associated with the white bull Zeus became before carrying Europa across the sea to Crete. Beneath that beautiful appearance was the strength of a god. I think about that when people mistake this sign’s love of pleasure for weakness. Taurus knows the power of holding its ground.

Tonight’s Full Moon at 2°46′ Taurus opposes the Scorpio Sun and squares Pluto in Aquarius. This brings intensity to questions of ownership, attachment, and control. Look closely at what you’ve been tolerating to feel secure, and what that security is actually costing you.

Venus, the ruler of Taurus, returns to Libra today while retrograde, and Mercury is now retrograde in Scorpio. We’re revisiting our relationships with money, desire, and reciprocity. Where are you pouring your resources? Are you being nourished by what you continue to feed?

Taurus is fixed earth. Its magic grows through patience, devotion, and tending to what we want to last. Working money magic beneath a Taurus Full Moon is a working for longevity, with the intention of building prosperity that can sustain us for years.

Tonight at 5:30 PM PT / 8:30 PM ET, we’re making money bowls together in my Patreon Full Moon ritual. Bring your intentions for the life you’re building. You deserve to enjoy what you work so hard to sustain.

SOLARY CUNNING CLASS - WEDS 30TH SEPT

Happy Monday, folks. In but two short days – on Wednesday 30th September – I will be delivering my brand new class, Solary Cunning, exploring the working-books of early modern British cunning-folk and analysing their conjurations, charms, and operations for working with the Sun. 

From timing to materia, golden fairy-flowers to images of yourself in gold (and what to use instead when gold is too costly…!), and from identifying thieves through dream to stopping gossip – not to mention “conjuring the sun” itself by streamlined resort to older medieval arcana – this class will deliver a host of traditional practices and approaches to working with the diurnal luminary of empowerment and thwarting malfeasance. 

Putting this class together has already enriched my perspectives and understandings on both planetary magic and cunning-craft, and as such I can happily advise this class to anyone interested in the intersections of astrological magic and folk sorcery, as well as those looking to dive deeper into techniques and workings collected in the personal spellbooks of pre-modern service magicians. 

You can read more about what we’ll be getting into and sign up to join us from the usual 🔗🌳 hub up top. The class will of course also be recorded, and sent out to all ticket holders a few days after the live session.

We at the museum would like to announce that after long consideration, we are changing our name to better reflect the museum and its collections. The museum will now be known as The Edinburgh Museum of Magic & Witchcraft.

The reason for the name change is for two reasons. One, many companies that provide services for business have regulations against “fortune-telling” and the beginning of this year our previous terminal software company cancelled our account with them because their AI-generated service picked up on the word Fortune-telling in the name of the museum. We don’t really want to see this happening again with the terminal software we are currently using now and the only way to combat this is to change the name of the museum.

Secondly, the team at the museum collectively came together and felt that although the term “fortune-telling” is acceptable in academia, its negative connotations does not reflect the items in the museum associated with divination and similar spiritual practices. There seems to be a bit of a witch hunt resurfacing regarding divination practices provided as a service, and governmental officials and companies seem to be following suit in this. I have seen esoteric shops being targeted in countries where old laws against “fortune-telling” and we want to stand in solidarity with other business that provide divination services and bring an awareness that these are a spiritual practice NOT Fortune-telling, and have been provided as a service to the community for hundreds of years. 

We have also updated our logo and now have tote bags you can purchase in our gift shop. Soon will be available to purchase on our website 😊

Would you rather visit your ancestors in the past or meet your descendants in the future? 

October and November are months of ancestral veneration. We tend our altars, prepare offerings, and spend time honoring our dead. This year, Venus retrograde in Scorpio brings questions of love and inheritance into that practice. Some of the beliefs we’re reconsidering have been in our families longer than anyone can remember.

With Mercury also in Scorpio, I’m interested in what we could learn if we could hear the stories firsthand. Family history changes depending on who is telling it. There are things people take to the grave that everyone else spends a lifetime trying to understand.

If you could sit down with an ancestor, what would you actually ask? Would you want to know how they practiced their magic? Who taught them? Would you tell them what happened to their children or homes? 

I wonder what they would make of us. Would they recognize something they had prayed for, or have some serious questions about what the hell we’re doing. 

Meeting our descendants would put us on the other side of that conversation. We would be answering questions about our beliefs, our choices, and things we never imagined anyone would remember.

That feels like a question worth sitting with this ancestor season. Would you go back, or would you go forward? 🤔🤔

GEOMANCY & THE MAGIC OF PLACE CLASS 

Happy Jupiterday folks. This coming Monday 26th October I will be delivering my new class, Worlding Points: Geomancy & the Magic of Place, in which we’ll be exploring how geomantic divination and spellcraft engages with the mysteries and magics of place, paying particular attention to planetary locations and the practical dirt sorceries we can do from there.

Geomancy is sometimes called the terrestrial sister art of astrology, for geomancers map the worldly events and influences of the Earth and Place just as our astrologer colleagues chart the astral virtues and effects of the Heavens and Time. 

As such, geomancy holds out a range of operative engagements with the land and its locales that can offer us incredibly useful and grounded methods and means to cohere and direct a range of influences, energies, and spirits: from surveying the specific sorts of places in which each of the sixteen geomantic figures are “at home” and thus may be indicated in a reading, to suggesting a range of beneficial modalities of spiritwork and spellcraft with those figural entities and influences. 

If you’ve ever wondered where you can bury a spell to best deploy and magnify its effects, or how you should dress or otherwise conduct yourself when gathering dirts for your charms and operations, or what offerings to leave where for planetary workings, this class is most definitely for you.

Here's the thing about The Lovers that surprises people: it's not primarily a romance card. Yes, it can point to love and partnership, but the deeper meaning is about choice. About standing at a crossroads and having to decide which path aligns with your authentic self. It's one of the most powerful cards in the deck because it's about integration, bringing together different parts of yourself into wholeness. 💕

The imagery usually shows two figures with an angel above them, and that's significant. The Lovers asks us to make choices that honor both our earthly desires and our higher values. It's not about picking passion over responsibility or vice versa. It's about finding the path where both can coexist. The choice that feels right in your gut and in your soul.

When The Lovers appears, pay attention to what decisions are weighing on you. What are you being asked to commit to? And here's the uncomfortable part: choosing one thing often means releasing another. The Lovers doesn't let us stay on the fence forever. At some point, we have to choose. ✨

The temples have fallen silent. The priesthoods have vanished. Empires have risen from dust and returned to it. Yet the current of the Ancient Wisdom has never ceased to flow.

From the shadowed sanctuaries of Egypt, where the mysteries of divine kingship, cosmic order, and the perfection of the soul were first clothed in symbol and ritual, there emerged a tradition not bound to any single creed or civilization. The outward forms changed with the centuries — pagan, Christian, Enlightenment, and secular, but the inner doctrine endured.

Freemasonry stands as one of the great vessels of that continuity. Neither a religion nor a relic of the past, it serves as a living repository of initiatic knowledge, preserving through allegory, architecture, geometry, and ceremonial drama those perennial truths once taught within the mystery schools of antiquity. The sacred eye, the pillars, the celestial vault, the working tools of the builder; all are fragments of a language far older than the modern world.

The Pharaoh and the Mason are separated by millennia, yet they stand beneath the same Light. One gazes upon the mysteries through the symbols of Egypt, the other through the symbolism of the Lodge. The garments differ; the wisdom remains.

For while nations, faiths, and philosophies pass through successive ages, the Brotherhood persists as a guardian of the hidden tradition, preserving the ember of ancient knowledge against the darkness of forgetfulness, carrying it from age to age until the seeker is prepared to receive it.

Lux ex Tenebris. Ordo ab Chao.
The forms of civilization change; the Mystery endures.

For years, Terra Keck has collected other people’s encounters with things that shouldn’t be there. The pattern she keeps finding isn’t in the encounters. It’s in what happens afterwards.

The encounters themselves barely change. Lights that move wrong. Small figures with big eyes and tiny mouths. The names shift across centuries -  fairies, angels, visitations, craft - but the shape of the experience holds, and so does the silence after it. Saying it out loud costs you something, and most people work that out fast.

Terra is an artist and a curatorial partner at Field Projects in Chelsea. She makes her drawings by erasing, building the image out of what she takes away, and she approaches all of it from the position that the universe is, at its core, benevolent.

She has one of her own, too. There’s a recording.

Somewhere in this conversation, she stops being the one studying it.

Would you rather visit your ancestors in the past or meet your descendants in the future? 

October and November are months of ancestral veneration. We tend our altars, prepare offerings, and spend time honoring our dead. This year, Venus retrograde in Scorpio brings questions of love and inheritance into that practice. Some of the beliefs we’re reconsidering have been in our families longer than anyone can remember.

With Mercury also in Scorpio, I’m interested in what we could learn if we could hear the stories firsthand. Family history changes depending on who is telling it. There are things people take to the grave that everyone else spends a lifetime trying to understand.

If you could sit down with an ancestor, what would you actually ask? Would you want to know how they practiced their magic? Who taught them? Would you tell them what happened to their children or homes? 

I wonder what they would make of us. Would they recognize something they had prayed for, or have some serious questions about what the hell we’re doing. 

Meeting our descendants would put us on the other side of that conversation. We would be answering questions about our beliefs, our choices, and things we never imagined anyone would remember.

That feels like a question worth sitting with this ancestor season. Would you go back, or would you go forward? 🤔🤔

𖦹 Hidden in the heart of the New Forest lies the magickal witch village of Burley. Famous for its many witchcraft shops and wild ponies, the village was once home to its most notable resident, Sybil Leek; a self professed white witch who in the 1950s could often be seen walking through Burley with her pet jackdaw, Mr Hotfoot Jackson, perched on her shoulder. 🐦‍⬛ 

𖦹 Sybil was born on 22nd February 1917, at "a crossroads where three rivers meet, in a wild and witch-ridden part of Staffordshire". Her mother was a psychic and her grandmother an astrologer who tutored her in the ways of magick. Whilst folk such as author H.G.Wells and occultist Aleister Crowley were frequent visitors to the family home, the latter she recalls teaching her poetry whilst mountain climbing. 

𖦹 After being initiated into a French coven, Sybil then spent some time living with the Romani before settling in Burley and opening an antiques shop. During this period she started the Horsa Coven, of which she was High Priestess, and she also gave covenofwitchesburley its name. 

𖦹 Burley though, was not to remain her home, and leaving England behind she moved to America and became a renowned author, writing nigh on 60 books on astrology and witchcraft. She also partnered with parapsychologist Hans Holzner and together they investigated cases of hauntings across America. 
Sybil left this world on 26th October 1982, and i'll leave you with an excerpt from her brilliant book Diary of a Witch ꩜🍃

Let’s make one thing clear from the start. God is everything, but religion, as most people know it, is something constructed. Not divine in its current form, but shaped over time by human hands with power and control in mind. History wasn’t just written, it was edited, filtered, and locked away until truth became distant and almost unrecognizable.

What we live in is not just a world, it’s a curated version of reality. Information was never meant to be fully free, because free information wakes people up. And once people wake up, the illusion begins to crack. That’s why truth is often hidden, complicated, or drowned in noise.

They didn’t just organize society, they divided perception. Borders were drawn not only on maps, but in minds. hermeticism.caption: Maymon, Demon King of the South. // According to the Grimoire of St. Cyprian, Maymon is one of the Four Demon Kings, and is attributed to the South. He is associated with a black bird, crowned and standing upon a branch, similar to the illustration found in Faust’s Magia Naturalis et Innaturalis. In Clavis Inferni, Maymon is placed in opposition to the Archangel Gabriel. He is also associated with sovereignty over other spirits, including Asmodeus, who is described as acting under his power. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Egyn, Demon King of the North. // According to the Grimoire of St. Cyprian, Egyn is one of the Four Demon Kings, and is attributed to the North. He is associated with a blue, crowned bear, representing the element of Earth. In Clavis Inferni, Egyn is placed in opposition to the Archangel Uriel. He is associated with knowledge of the natural world, hidden things, and the revelation of secrets. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Fleur-de-lis ankh. // I worked on this piece a few years ago when I first moved to New Orleans. Originally associated with the French monarchy, the fleur-de-lis arrived in Louisiana during the French colonial period and eventually became one of the city’s most recognizable emblems. The ankh symbolizes everlasting life, while the fleur-de-lis evokes New Orleans’ French heritage. The earliest versions of the fleur-de-lis were represented as scarab beetles, which the Egyptians regarded as sacred symbols of rebirth, renewal, and spiritual enlightenment. The two symbols combined celebrate New Orleans as a crossroads of history and spirituality. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

The Thoth deck. // I recently had the chance to see Lady Frieda Harris’s original paintings at the Morgan Library. Developed in collaboration with Aleister Crowley for the Thoth Tarot, Harris’s study of Rudolf Steiner’s Anthroposophy and projective synthetic geometry influenced the development of the Thoth deck, shaping its distinctive use of form, movement, and color. Seeing the paintings in person and on a large scale was a striking experience. It gave me a renewed appreciation for one of the most influential works of the modern Western esoteric tradition.

Anu, Lord of the Constellations. // Known as the Sky Father, King of the Gods, Lord of the Constellations, Anu is the divine personification of the sky, supreme God and father of all the deities in the Mesopotamian religion. He was believed to be the supreme source of all authority, for the other gods and for all mortal rulers, and he is described in one text as the one “who contains the entire universe”. He is identified with the north ecliptic pole centered in the constellation Draco. His symbol is the Dingir, a star shaped ideogram that represents the heavens. The original association of divinity is thus with the “bright” or “shining” stars in the sky. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Baphomet. // “They have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which I did not command, and it did not come into My mind.” —Jer. 7:31 // Winter Solstice, the shortest day of the year, was linked with Capricornus in the Zodiac. Eliphas Levi studied thus intently because of its connection with ceremonial magic, identifying it with Baphomet, the ass-headed idol of the Templar Knights. Still, it was greatly misunderstood. He succeeded in identifying the goat with Pan, portrayed as Pan Pangenitor, the All-Begetter. It is the male creative force, the goat leaping with lust upon the summit of the earth. It is also refers to all gods containing these correspondences, such as Sheitan or Satan. Essential to the symbolism is the surroundings, the barren places, especially high places, mountaintops. The Old Testament is full of stories of the temptation of kings who worshiped in “high places”, desolate summits uncontaminated by the deeds of men. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Heart, skin, and flesh. // The keys to the construction of the Enochian Lamen are in the condensation of the 12x7 table containing the letters of the names of the seven planetary Heptarchic Kings and their Princes. From the outside in, the Lamen is divided into three sections: the flesh, heart, and skin. The flesh is added to the perimeter of the Lamen, then the heart to the corners of the inner square. The skin is added to the corners of the diamond square, and the remaining letters of the 12x7 table are woven in between. As the Table of Practice conciliates Heaven and earth, so does the Lamen placed over the heart conciliate the magician to the Holy Table. // Gold, link in profile.

Xeper signet ring. // I worked on this ring a few years ago. This signet ring features the hieroglyphs of Xeper: the scarab god of transformation and remanifestation, the mouth, the spoken word that creates and the scroll, the written word that preserves. I’ve always found something magical in the process of crafting and making things by hand. The artificer transforms thought into form. Taking an idea and slowly bringing it into existence mirrors the process of creating experiences. In creating something, we also create opportunities to change and become. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

What you are observing is the diagram of the Tree of Life of the Kabbalah, the fundamental structure of Jewish mystical cosmology, later adopted and reinterpreted within Western Hermetic alchemy. The Tree is composed of ten Sephiroth (divine emanations) connected by twenty-two paths, corresponding to the letters of the Hebrew alphabet and, in esoteric tradition, to the Major Arcana of the Tarot.

At the summit stands the Supernal Triad — Kether, Chokmah, and Binah — which represents the primordial process of emanation: from pure Will to dynamic Wisdom and finally to formative Understanding. Descending along the three Pillars (Mercy, Severity, and Balance), energy progressively condenses until it reaches Malkuth, the Kingdom, corresponding to the material plane.

For the alchemist, this scheme is not merely metaphysical speculation; it is an operative map of inner transformation. The Sephiroth reflect states of consciousness, psychic forces, and stages of refinement of the Self, while the paths indicate the trials and integrations necessary for ascent. To study this diagram is to understand that the alchemical Work — Solve et Coagula — is not simply the transmutation of metals, but the reintegration of the human being into its transcendent origin.
